fields.name: oauth_client_id
fields.description: Non-secret OAuth 2.0 (3LO) client ID copied from https://developer.atlassian.com/console/myapps/ after selecting the app > Settings > Authentication details > Client ID; an alphanumeric value, and blank means authorization and refresh cannot start.

fields.name: oauth_client_secret
fields.description: Secret OAuth 2.0 (3LO) client secret copied from https://developer.atlassian.com/console/myapps/ > the app > Settings > Authentication details > Secret; store it only in this credential field, and blank means authorization and refresh cannot start.

fields.name: access_token
fields.description: Secret short-lived access token returned by Atlassian after consent; Dex derives it automatically and refreshes it before its one-hour expiry, so never enter it manually, and blank means Connect has not completed.

fields.name: refresh_token
fields.description: Secret rotating refresh token returned because the connection requests offline_access; Atlassian disables each refresh token once it issues the next, so Dex stores every replacement atomically, and blank means reauthorization is required.

steps: Choose Create > OAuth 2.0 integration, name the app, and accept the developer terms; one app can serve every Dex connection.

Open Permissions, choose Add next to Jira API, then Configure, and add the classic scopes read:jira-work and write:jira-work; Dex also requests offline_access so Atlassian issues a rotating refresh token.
Open Authorization, choose Configure next to OAuth 2.0 (3LO), paste the exact Redirect URI shown below into Callback URL, and choose Save changes.
Open Settings and copy Client ID and Secret into the fields below; the secret is sensitive.

Choose Connect, pick the Jira site the Flows work in on the Atlassian consent screen, and choose Accept. The app stays private to its owner until Distribution > Enable sharing is on, and a refresh token unused for 90 days requires reconnecting.
